```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Buyer and sales cycle fit 90 days better. Idea A sells to an engineering team lead on per-seat pricing, with a cited anchor of $8–10/seat/month from Lody. Idea B's highest-value buyer, banks, has a cited 6–18 month sales cycle and needs SOC 2 Type II before outbound, which rules it out within 90 days.",
    "Regulatory exposure is lower. Idea A's brief lists security posture (SOC2-type attestation, retention policy) as an adoption hurdle for enterprise pilots, not a legal barrier. Idea B's brief cites biometric-privacy risk that privacy-preserving design does not remove: BIPA, a $650M Facebook settlement, and Worldcoin bans or investigations. That risk applies even in the self-serve segment if any liveness or biometric signal is used.",
    "Both markets are crowded with free tiers. In Idea A, Slack Code is free and bundled into every Slack plan, a $0 anchor for the core feature. Still, Idea A's brief shows paid workspace-only pricing among small players (Lody, Warp Business at $45–50/user/month). Idea B's competitors already hold the named enterprise logos (Zoom with World ID, Incognia with 1B+ devices), leaving only a self-serve segment with at least four free-tier rivals.",
    "Demand evidence is anecdotal in both. Idea A's two quotes come from people describing the exact workflow pain the product targets. Idea B's quotes are a consumer on Reddit, who is not the payer, and a competitor's executive.",
    "Idea A's case leans on its own unsourced claims, which count as missing. These are that the product is buildable solo in six weeks and that sales/support/analyst demand is significant. Its case should be judged on an engineering-team wedge only."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence leans on a quote from Trevor Traina, Chief Business Officer of Tools for Humanity (World ID), a direct competitor. It is vendor marketing about the Zoom partnership, not evidence that any reachable payer would buy from a new solo entrant. Close behind is the case-for claim that a solo founder can assemble a credible verification API in weeks. It carries no source, so it counts as missing, though it carries the whole feasibility argument.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs show crowded markets with free incumbents, and both rely on thin, anecdotal demand evidence. Neither shows a validated paying wedge. Idea A wins mainly because Idea B carries documented, structural blockers: long bank sales cycles, compliance prerequisites, and biometric legal risk. Idea A's main threats (free bundling by Slack, security-depth expectations) are commercial rather than regulatory. If Idea A's unsourced six-week build claim fails, its advantage narrows considerably."
}
```
